# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the
  weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level
  readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and
run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and
assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the
GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene:
  round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a
  level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests
  (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart,
  every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling
  real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert
  `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the
  duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not
  duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD;
  otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to
  name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay
  or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record
  any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable
  under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle
  **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an
  optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout;
  keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under
  parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a
  single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way
  to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public
  restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent /
  `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry`
  and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb
  (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace
  `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration
  tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining
  core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals`
  and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the
shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview
when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each
apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and
the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated
  gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?**
  — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title
  and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
  (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?**
  — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is
  identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the
  description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level
  path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7
  behaviour is fully observable?**
  — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the
  default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require
  observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and
  demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the
  threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or
  a gym-local panel?**
  — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` /
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the
  shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the
  established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?**
  — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the
  gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence.
  Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic
  matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal
  relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.
data.title: Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.

- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

## Goal
Evaluate whether consumable temporary grants should be modelled as a distinct power-up type/category rather than as a level that is temporarily raised. This is an *exploratory* task — no code behaviour change is committed until a design decision is made and accepted.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.

## Problem

`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` test **AC4 — the victory celebration is destroyed on SHUTDOWN (no leaks)** (around line 3864) failed once during a full-suite run on 2026-10-07 while the machine was under heavy multi-agent load, then passed on an immediate re-run.

The test waits a real `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS + 500` ms via `setTimeout` and then asserts the victory effects are destroyed. Under CPU/timer contention the hold can take longer, so the assertion races the transition.

- First run: `Test Files 1 failed | 151 passed`, `Tests 1 failed | 3509 passed` (failure at `PlayScene.test.ts` ~line 3883, `expect(effect.active).toBe(false)`).
- Immediate re-run: 152 files / 3510 tests passed.

## Expected behaviour

The test should be deterministic regardless of machine load (use fake timers / pump the scene clock rather than a wall-clock `setTimeout`, or wait on the scene state instead of a fixed delay).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The AC4 test no longer depends on a wall-clock `setTimeout` window that can be missed under load.
- AC2: The test passes repeatedly under load (e.g. run the full suite 3x on a loaded machine).
- AC3: No other PlayScene tests regress.

This is unrelated to the capture epic (the capture changes touch only `scripts/`).

# Intake Brief — Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old

## Problem statement

AI_Hell's enemy roster (E1–E7) is a coherent but self-contained set of
formations. It does not yet deliberately mine the **classic arcade era** for
signature, instantly-recognisable enemy behaviours. This epic researches that
era and turns the best candidates into implementable work items, so the game
can grow a distinctive "arcade homage" roster without ad-hoc, un-scoped enemy
requests.

## Users

- **As the game designer**, I want a researched, curated catalogue of classic
  arcade enemy behaviours adapted to AI_Hell's neon-vector rules, so that new
  enemy work starts from a clear design brief rather than a one-line wish.
- **As an implementing agent/developer**, I want each selected enemy to have
  its own work item with a user story, testable ACs, predicted key files and a
  plan that follows the existing data-driven enemy convention, so I can
  implement it without re-deriving the design.
- **As the producer**, I want the candidates that were considered but not
  selected recorded, so the roster can be expanded later without redoing the
  research.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A research document `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` exists and catalogues at least 5 and at most 8 selected classic arcade enemy archetypes, recording for each its source game, original behaviour, adaptation to AI_Hell's neon-vector code-drawn no-enemy-collision rules, and why it was selected.
- The research document includes a considered but not selected section listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
- One child work item exists per selected archetype, each containing a user story, measurable and testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and a plan that follows section 8.6 Adding a new enemy in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and each child references this epic and the research document.
- Each selected archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven pipeline, whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and give its enemy difficulty scoring inputs for movement, fire and health factors.
- Each selected archetype's notes name the gym scenes that will exercise it, existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym, to satisfy the gym-to-game parity rule.
- Validation checks the research document recommendations against existing engine constraints so every selected archetype maps to an existing or explicitly-planned formation/shot-pattern registry entry, and every child work item carries explicit unit-test acceptance criteria.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** — no external art assets
  (GDD §7.2).
- **Gym↔game parity** — an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a
  gym and the game; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`. Enforced by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs
  assertion (AGENTS.md).
- **Data-driven enemies** — tuning is data, not code; archetypes are rows in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN). A genuinely new entity is
  only justified when the existing formation/shot registries cannot express it.
- **"Enemies are the bullets" design** (GDD §2.4) and **no enemy–enemy
  collisions** (GDD §2.6).
- **Behaviours must be adaptable to a top-down free-2D arena** — the original
  arcade games are lane/axis-based; the brief must state how each archetype is
  translated (or note where translation is not faithful).
- **Scope is research + design + child-item creation.** This epic does not
  itself implement the enemies; each selected archetype's implementation is its
  own child work item.

## Existing state

- **Enemy catalog** (GDD §4.1, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1):
  E1 Scout, E2 Diver, E3 Tank, E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, E6 Asteroid, E7 Harvester,
  plus the multi-phase Boss.
- **Enemy implementation guide** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  documents the shared core scene library, the CSV pipeline (§8), and the
  "adding a new enemy" checklist (§8.6).
- **Data-driven pipeline**: `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`, `src/core/configTypes.ts`,
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`,
  `src/utils/enemyShotPatterns.ts`, `src/utils/formations.ts`.
- **Difficulty scoring**: `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` (absolute 0–100 index;
  movement/fire/health factors), pinned by
  `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.
- **Gym surface**: single reusable `GymEnemies` scene + `GymIndex`; new CSV rows
  appear automatically.
- **Precedent**: E6 Asteroid (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) is already an arcade homage
  built as a non-formation roamer with a split helper — a model for how far a

# Intake Brief — Bot is more gentle on the thrusters (AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A)

## Problem statement

The attract/demo bot's human-like thrust layer holds every forward-thrust press
for a fixed random band (200–225 ms normally, up to 400 ms on a long-travel
leg). This makes the bot's thruster "on" runs a little longer than a human's
and contributes to a slightly mechanical, over-eager feel. The producer wants
the bot to be a little gentler on the thrusters by shortening each press's
**on** time by a random **1–5%**.

## Users

- **Attract-mode viewer / operator:** watches the demo run and perceives the
  bot as a believable human pilot rather than a thruster-abusing machine.
- **Gameplay designers:** tune bot feel through one shared module without
  hunting for magic numbers.

Example user stories:

- *As an operator watching the attract demo, I want the bot to make slightly
  shorter, less mechanical thrust bursts, so that the demo reads as human play.*
- *As a designer, I want the gentle-thrust reduction to be a single documented
  tunable pair, so that I can adjust the feel without touching the governor
  logic.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each forward-thrust press duration is reduced by a random factor drawn
  uniformly from **1%–5%** (inclusive of the configured bounds). With the
  default caps this shortens a normal press from the 200–225 ms band to
  ≈190–222.75 ms and a long-travel press from the 400 ms cap to ≈380 ms;
  unit-tested.
- AC2: The reduction is drawn **per press** and is reproducible for a given
  governor seed (a run-seeded governor produces an identical reduction
  sequence across two instances with the same seed); unit-tested.
- AC3: Continuous desired thrust still holds the thruster **on** for every tick
  (the reduction must not introduce off-gaps); existing continuous-thrust test
  remains green.
- AC4: The reduction bounds live in the shared `BotHumanInputTunables` module
  (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) as documented min/max percent tunables with
  defaults `0.01`/`0.05`; no scattered magic numbers.
- AC5: Documentation is updated to describe the gentler thrust — the demo-bot
  subsection in `docs/Game Design Document.md` and the `botHumanLike.ts`
  module doc both note the 1–5% random reduction of press "on" time.
- AC6: At least one new automated test validates the reduction band and
  per-press randomness; full project test suite, typecheck and build must pass
  with the change.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the change surgical: only the thrust-press duration draw is affected;
  the chosen heading/target, reaction cadence, W/A/D key limits, and
  forward-model braking reflex are unchanged.
- No new dependency; keep the deterministic mulberry32 RNG already used for
  per-press jitter (do not introduce `Math.random()`).
- The reduction must be a *reduction only* (never extend a press), so the bot
  becomes gentler, not more aggressive.
- Single source of truth for tunables (`BOT_HUMAN_INPUT_TUNABLES`).

## Existing state

`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` implements the human-like input governor. In
`BotInputGovernor.resolveThrustPress`, a new press duration is drawn as:

```ts
const maxMs = longTravel ? thrustPressMaxMsLong : thrustPressMaxMs;
const span = Math.max(0, maxMs - thrustPressMinMs);
this.thrustPressRemainingMs = thrustPressMinMs + this.random() * span;
```

Defaults: `thrustPressMinMs: 200`, `thrustPressMaxMs: 225`,
`thrustPressMaxMsLong: 400`. The drawn duration is the thruster's "on" time.
`resolveThrustPress` is unit-tested in `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`
(`human-like thrust presses (AC15/AC16)` suite), and the GDD demo-bot
subsection documents the 200–225 / 400 ms bands.

## Desired change

After drawing the base press duration, apply a per-press random reduction of
1–5%:

```ts
const baseMs = thrustPressMinMs + this.random() * span;
const reduction =
  thrustPressGentleMinPct +
  this.random() * (thrustPressGentleMaxPct - thrustPressGentleMinPct);
this.thrustPressRemainingMs = baseMs * (1 - reduction);
```

Add the two bounds to `BotHumanInputTunables` and
`BOT_HUMAN_INPUT_TUNABLES`, document them, and update the GDD demo-bot
subsection and module doc.

**Interpretation note (documented assumption):** the phrase *"reduce their
'on' time by between 1 and 5% (random)"* is read as reducing each thrust-press
**hold duration** by a per-press random 1–5%. This is the only "on" time in
the bot's thrust path. The alternative reading — inserting random off-gaps
into the thrust duty cycle — is explicitly **out of scope** for this item and
recorded as a risk below; the producer can request it during review.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — add `thrustPressGentleMinPct` /
  `thrustPressGentleMaxPct` tunables and apply the per-press reduction in
  `resolveThrustPress`; update module/documentation comments.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts` — extend the "human-like thrust presses"
  suite with reduction-band and per-press-randomness/determinism tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — demo-bot subsection: note the 1–5% random
  reduction of thrust-press on-time.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — Demo bot: human-like input limits (W/A/D, reaction
  time) and complete the hold-full upgrade choice** (completed) — introduced
  the governor, the human reaction cadence, and the 200–225 / 400 ms thrust
  press bands this item tunes.
- **AH-0MUXYOV4C008MV0L — Demo bot movement goals: minerals > power-ups >
  enemies > asteroids** (completed) — the steering/priority behaviour that
  produces the thrust decisions.
- **AH-0MUY08V6W001SJJN — Deterministic run seeding and seed plumbing**
  (completed) — the run seed that re-seeds the governor's per-press RNG, which
  keeps the new reduction deterministic per run.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` § demo/attract bot ("Predictive braking
  (AC10)" bullet) — documents the current thrust-press durations.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (interpretation):** "on time" = thrust-press hold duration
  (see Desired change). If the producer intended a duty-cycle gap instead,
  this item's scope is wrong and should be re-defined before implementation.
- **Risk — negligible visible effect:** because a press is continuously
  renewed while the live `thrust` flag stays `true`, the reduction mainly
  shortens the *overhang* after the forward model decides to coast. A 1–5%
  change is deliberately subtle; the demo may need an audition to confirm the
  feel is meaningfully gentler. Mitigation: make the bounds tunable so the
  band can be widened without a code change.
- **Risk — scope creep:** while in the governor it is tempting to also retune
  reaction time or the press caps. Those are out of scope; file separate work
  items if required.
- **Failure mode:** if the reduction were applied as an extension or with an
  inverted sign, the bot would thrust *harder*. AC1/AC3 pin the direction and
  the no-gap behaviour.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed context ("reduce their 'on' time by
between 1 and 5% (random)") plus repo/worklog search resolved the target
mechanism unambiguously — the human-like thrust-press hold duration in
`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`. The one interpretation decision (press duration vs
duty-cycle gap) is recorded as a documented assumption in "Desired change"
and flagged under "Risks & assumptions".

- Q: *What is the bot's "on" time that should be reduced?* — Answer (agent,
  from repo evidence): the forward-thrust press hold duration drawn in
  `BotInputGovernor.resolveThrustPress` (200–225 ms, 400 ms long-travel);
  this is the only thruster "on" time in the path. Source:
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` lines ~360–385.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHF3SJL009T2QL** – Wire thruster audio in Player.ts (completed)
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** – Alternative player control (completed)
- **AH-0MUYOBU4F003EYRP** – [test-failure] src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts > Demo mode integration (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P) > AC1 — the demo bot drives the ship through the live shared input path — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muxxq1mn002rxgb, ac1, ac10, ac15, ac16 (+258 more)
- `README.md` — matched: ac1, ac10, ac15, ac16, ac3 (+254 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5, add (+215 more)

# Add a reverse thruster to the Asteroids ship control scheme — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Under the shipped **Asteroids** control scheme the ship can only thrust *forward* (W / ↑) and turn (A / ←, D / →): there is no way to slow or back away while holding a heading. Players must spin the whole ship around to change speed. We want a **reverse thruster** — a held retro-thrust opposite the ship's facing direction, bound to **S / ↓** — that is individually tunable and can be switched off completely.

## Users

- **Player** (primary): needs an intuitive way to brake/back up without turning the ship, with the ability to disable the extra control if they prefer classic Asteroids handling.
- **Developer / designer**: needs to tune the reverse thruster (or turn it off) from the Player gym and persist it with the rest of the ship config.

Example user stories:

- As a player, holding **S / ↓** while flying forward decelerates my ship (retro-thrust) and, if held, accelerates me backwards in the direction opposite my nose.
- As a player who dislikes the reverse thruster, I can switch it **off completely** so S / ↓ do nothing and my handling matches the classic scheme.
- As a designer, I can tune the reverse acceleration and reverse max speed independently of the forward values, live in the Player gym, and see the ship's nose retro-thruster flame while reversing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Reverse input & physics (Asteroids scheme only).** Under the Asteroids scheme, holding **S** or **↓** applies continuous acceleration **opposite** the ship's facing direction at a configurable reverse acceleration; releasing the key restores the normal friction behaviour. When no reverse key is held the ship behaves exactly as today. The 4-directional scheme is unchanged.
2. **AC2 — Individually customisable & persisted.** Reverse thrust is configured through `ShipConfig` with a master **on/off boolean** plus dedicated tunables — a **reverse thrust acceleration** and a **reverse max speed** — independent of the forward `thrustAcceleration` / `maxSpeed` values. The values round-trip through `src/data/ship-config.csv` and the config store, with sane defaults for legacy configs that predate the fields.
3. **AC3 — Can be turned off completely.** When the reverse toggle is disabled, S / ↓ produce **no** reverse acceleration, **no** reverse flame and no other movement side effect; forward thrust and turning are unaffected.
4. **AC4 — Reverse VFX.** Reverse thrust renders a dedicated forward-facing **nose retro-thruster** flame that grows/decays using the existing animated-flame model and rotates with the hull; only engines that are firing are drawn.
5. **AC5 — Gym control.** The Player gym exposes the on/off toggle and the reverse tunables (checkbox + sliders), applies changes live, and persists them via the existing Save path.
6. **AC6 — Demo bot unaffected.** The human-like demo governor continues never to emit reverse input (W/A/D only); `AsteroidsInput.reverse` is always `false` from the bot.
7. **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated (at minimum the GDD controls table and §2.2 movement, plus code comments), including a note that the reverse thruster exists, its default binding and how to disable it.
8. **AC8 — Tests.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes, and new/updated tests cover: reverse physics (acceleration, clamp, friction on release), the disabled-toggle no-op, config/CSV round-trip and legacy defaults, engine-selection/VFX for reverse, input mapping for S/↓, and the bot never emitting reverse.

## Constraints

- Applies to the **Asteroids** control scheme only (`controlScheme: 'asteroids'`); the 4-directional scheme already has a down/backward thrust and must not change.
- Must preserve **gym↔game parity**: reverse physics and VFX live in the shared core (`src/utils/movementModel.ts` + `src/entities/Player.ts`) and are consumed identically by the game and gyms — no divergent copy.
- Must be **backward compatible** with existing persisted `ShipConfig` / `ship-config.csv` data (missing fields fall back to defaults).
- **Depends on** the separate Teleport-automation item AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC: once Teleport is automatic, S / ↓ are free for reverse thrust and the manual-teleport key handling is removed.

## Existing state

- **Scheme/input:** `AsteroidsInputHandler.mapInput` (`src/utils/movementModel.ts`) maps W/↑ → `forward`, A/← → `turnLeft`, D/→ → `turnRight`; **S/↓ are deliberately excluded** (S is a 4-directional backward-thrust binding only).
- **Model:** `AsteroidsModel.tick` applies forward acceleration along `facing`, friction when `!forward`, a `maxSpeed` clamp and edge wrap. There is no reverse acceleration.
- **Engines/VFX:** `Player._engines()` defines the Asteroids engines `main` (rear), `leftSide`, `rightSide`; `getEngineActivity` returns them for forward/turn input, and `Player._updateFlames` animates each. No nose/retro engine exists.
- **Config:** `ShipConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`) holds `thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`, `controlScheme`, and the `asteroidsRotation*` fields; defaults in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`; CSV codec + `SHIP_COLUMN_ORDER` in `src/core/csv.ts`; shipped values in `src/data/ship-config.csv`.
- **Gym:** `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` renders one slider per numeric field (`SLIDER_RANGES`) with live apply + Save; there is no boolean/checkbox control yet.
- **Teleport conflict:** S (the `layerDrop` binding) and a hardcoded ↓ fallback currently activate a stored Teleport on key-down (`CombatScene._handleTeleport`). This is being removed by AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC (Teleport becomes automatic like Phase Shift), which this item depends on.

## Desired change

- Add `reverse: boolean` to `AsteroidsInput`; have `AsteroidsInputHandler` read **S** and **↓** for it.
- In `AsteroidsModel`, when reverse is held **and** the reverse thruster is enabled, apply `-cos(facing) * reverseAcceleration * dt` / `-sin(facing) * reverseAcceleration * dt`; gate friction on "no forward and no reverse input"; keep the existing clamp/wrap.
- Clamp the speed reachable under reverse thrust to the configurable **reverse max speed** — without abruptly braking pre-existing faster forward momentum (exact clamp semantics pinned by a unit test).
- Add a `nose` (retro) engine port to the Asteroids engine layout that fires when reversing, with an animated flame consistent with the other engines.
- Extend `ShipConfig` + defaults + CSV codec + `ship-config.csv` with `asteroidsReverseEnabled` (boolean), `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed`.
- Add the toggle + sliders to `GymPlayer` and cover the new behaviour with tests.
- Update the GDD (§2.2 movement, controls table) and code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — add `reverse` to `AsteroidsInput`; map S/↓ in `AsteroidsInputHandler`; apply reverse acceleration + clamp in `AsteroidsModel.tick`; return the nose engine from `getEngineActivity`; gate on the config toggle.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — add the `nose` retro-thruster `EnginePortDef` to the Asteroids layout and its flame rendering/animation.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the three new `ShipConfig` fields.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — default `asteroidsReverseEnabled`, `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration`, `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend `SHIP_COLUMN_ORDER`, parse/serialise/validate the boolean and numbers.
- `src/data/ship-config.csv` — add the new columns/values to the shipped row.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — add the on/off checkbox and reverse sliders (and their ranges).
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — keep `reverse: false` in the emitted `AsteroidsInput` (and the frozen idle input).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — controls table + §2.2 movement update.
- Tests — `src/utils/movementModel.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts` / `configDefaults.test.ts` / `configStore*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts`, `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`, and the parity guards `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / `gymParityDocs.test.ts` if they assert the input shape.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC** — Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust) — **dependency (blocks this item)**.
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** — Alternative player control (introduced the Asteroids scheme, `AsteroidsInput`, engine layout).
- **AH-0MTFORPJ2003RWWQ** — Asteroids directional VFX improvements (key-specific engine selection: forward→main, turn→side).
- **AH-0MUNS42NA000N41U** — More precise turn controls (the closed-form angular ramp in `AsteroidsModel`).
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ / AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** — Demo bot uses the ship's asteroid controls and is limited to human-like W/A/D.
- **AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620** — Player thruster SFX (`getEngineSoundLevel`); check reverse interacts sensibly with the hum.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: key-map conflict (mitigated).** S/↓ previously activated Teleport. Mitigated by making Teleport automatic in the prerequisite item; this item owns S/↓ only once that lands.
- **Risk: reverse clamp could feel like sudden braking.** Applying a reverse-specific speed cap to pre-existing faster forward momentum would jerk the ship. Mitigation: clamp only the reverse-accelerated speed (or use the larger of current speed / cap) and pin the semantics with a unit test.

# Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want the boss to move in a figure-of-8 so the encounter is dynamic and I have to track my shots; as a developer I want the motion implemented once so `PlayScene` and every boss gym stay in parity.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC3.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: `applyFormationPosition()` is a static `setPosition(baseX, baseY)`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_advanceBoss(dt)` calls `boss.update(this.time.now, dt*1000, GAME_WIDTH, GAME_HEIGHT)` for **both** the game and `GymBoss` — the correct shared per-frame home for motion.
- `GymFormationScene` calls `entity.applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, dt, ...)` on its boss each tick.

## Desired change

1. In the shared boss core, trace a Gerono lemniscate (figure-8) about the boss's spawn **anchor**:
   `theta = 2*PI * elapsedMs / BOSS_MOVE_PERIOD_MS`, `x = anchorX + BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_X * sin(theta)`,
   `y = anchorY + BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_Y * sin(2*theta)`.
   Export `BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_X = 120`, `BOSS_MOVE_AMPLITUDE_Y = 60`, `BOSS_MOVE_PERIOD_MS = 8000`.
2. Accumulate motion time in `Boss.update(...)` (from `delta`) and set the boss position there, so both scenes get identical motion via `CombatScene._advanceBoss`.
3. Change `applyFormationPosition()` to set the **anchor** (not teleport the container), so the gym's per-frame call cannot fight the figure-8.
4. Clamp the traced position to the playfield bounds so the boss never leaves the screen.
5. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live `x`/`y`; the health bar does not move (delivered by the sibling health-bar task).

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — motion constants, state, `update()`, `applyFormationPosition()`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — confirm `_advanceBoss` drives motion for both scenes.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts` — traced-position and bounded-amplitude tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — gym motion parity.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a deterministic `delta`, the boss position follows the lemniscate about its anchor with peak amplitudes ≈120 px horizontal and ≈60 px vertical and a full cycle of ≈8 s.
- The boss x/y stay within the playfield bounds across a full cycle.
- Calling `applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, ...)` sets the anchor without overriding the live figure-8 position.
- The boss's live position is used for hit detection; the health bar's screen position is unchanged while the boss moves.
- Motion is implemented once in shared core (attributable to the sibling health-bar task that keeps the bar static).

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC3) **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.

# Report script counts soft-deleted children

**discovered-from:AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2**

## Problem

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) shows an incorrect **Children** count when a parent has soft-deleted children.

- `wl delete <id>` is a **soft delete** — it sets `status=deleted` and `deletedBy`, and the item remains visible via `wl show <parent> --children`.
- `wl list --parent <id>` correctly **excludes** deleted items.
- `render_report.py` (`render_from_wl`) counts `len(data["children"])` from `wl show --children`, so it **includes** the tombstones.

Observed on AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2: 7 active children + 6 soft-deleted coverage-gap children reported as `Children: 13`; `wl list --parent` correctly reports 7.

## Expected behaviour

The report's child count matches the active child set — i.e. it excludes items with `status=deleted` (or `deletedBy` set). Ideally the shared `wl show --children` behaviour and the report agree with `wl list --parent`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a parent with children.
2. `wl delete <one-child> --json` (soft delete).
3. Run `python3 skill/report/scripts/render_report.py <parent-id> --skill-name plan ...`.
4. Observe the **Children** count includes the deleted child.

## Suggested fix

Filter deleted children in `render_from_wl` before counting (e.g. `[c for c in children if c.get("status") != "deleted" and not c.get("deletedBy")]`), or make `wl show --children` exclude deleted items consistently with `wl list --parent`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report's **Children** count excludes soft-deleted items.
- A test covers a parent with a mix of active and soft-deleted children.
- Behaviour is consistent with `wl list --parent`.
